page: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv6 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled with 5669 GB of local disk capacity, and the instance supports Premium Storage. No GPUs are present on this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities, with the Geekbench multi-core score and Passmark CPU score both ranking in the top tier (top 10%). The processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), contribute to top-tier performance in extended instruction tests and image processing. Single-core performance, as measured by stress-ng and bzip3 decompression, falls within the average range, indicating that the server's primary strength lies in parallelized execution. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks consistently rank in the strong category, though the overall Passmark memory score remains average.

With high local storage capacity and strong multi-threaded performance, the D96ds_v6 is suited for database operations, static web serving, and software compilation. It demonstrates top-tier throughput in static web serving and strong performance in Redis SET operations. For machine learning workloads, the CPU-based LLM inference speeds for prompt processing are strong across small, medium, and large models, though text generation speeds for large models drop to average. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of dedicated vCPUs and substantial local storage capacity provide a consolidated resource profile for enterprise workloads without the added cost of specialized GPU hardware.
